questions.question: Describe how Germany and Berlin were divided after 1945 and why the Allies disagreed about Germany's future.
questions.expected_answer: Germany was divided into four zones (US south, Britain north-west, France west, USSR east); Berlin, about 160 km inside the Soviet zone, into four sectors, under an Allied Control Council (four Ds: denazification, demilitarisation, democratisation, decentralisation). The USSR wanted Germany weak, took reparations and backed the SED (1946). The US and Britain wanted recovery for Europe and against communism, stopped reparations from their zones (1946), formed Bizonia (1 January 1947), then Trizonia, with Marshall aid.

questions.question: Explain the causes, events and results of the Berlin Blockade and Airlift.
questions.expected_answer: Cause: Western currency reform (Deutsche Mark, June 1948) and plans for a West German state. On 24 June 1948 the USSR cut road, rail and canal routes to West Berlin (about two million people, food for about five weeks). The West flew in supplies via air corridors (Operation Vittles; Tempelhof, Gatow, Tegel), over 270 000 flights and about 2,3 million tonnes, mostly coal, with South African crews among others. Stalin lifted it on 12 May 1949. Results: Western propaganda victory, NATO (April 1949), FRG (23 May 1949) and GDR (7 October 1949).

questions.question: Explain why the Berlin Wall was built in 1961 and describe its effects.
questions.expected_answer: West Germany's economic miracle contrasted with East German shortages, collectivisation and Stasi repression (1953 uprising crushed). About 2,7 million East Germans, many skilled, left via open Berlin by 1961 (about 30 000 in July 1961), a brain drain and embarrassment. Khrushchev pressured Kennedy (Vienna, June 1961). On 13 August 1961 the border was sealed with barbed wire, then concrete (about 155 km around West Berlin). Effects: families divided, death strip, at least 140 deaths (Peter Fechter 1962), escapes by tunnel and balloon; a symbol of the Cold War (Kennedy 1963, Reagan 1987).
